hints: Start with the pond 1 observations - high tadpole density but low food, and almost no intermediates left. What does survival of only the two opposite types tell you about who is winning and who is losing?

Think about why intermediates lose when food is scarce. Compare a specialist with smooth mouthparts and long intestine or large jaws and short intestine, with a jack-of-all-trades that is not as efficient at either food.
Recall the name for selection that pushes a population toward both extremes at once, and link it to intense competition and limited food acting as the selection pressure.
walkthrough:
Picture Life in Pond 1**
Imagine many tadpoles crowded together with very little detritus, algae or fairy shrimp to go round. Every tadpole is competing for the same limited food, so only the most efficient feeders get enough to grow and survive to reproduce.

Why Specialists Win and Intermediates Lose**
Detritus feeders have smooth mouthparts, small jaw muscles and long intestines ideal for digesting detritus and algae. Carnivores have teeth-like mouthparts, large jaw muscles and short intestines ideal for catching and digesting shrimp. Intermediates are medium at everything, so they are outcompeted for both food types by the specialists and starve.

Naming the Pattern**
When both opposite extremes increase in frequency and the middle type decreases, this is disruptive selection, also called diversifying selection. The selection pressure here is lack of food leading to intense intraspecific competition.

Final answer: Disruptive / diversifying selection; extremes (detritus feeders and carnivores) are selected for / survive and intermediates are selected against / die; due to high / intense competition and limited food as selection pressure.

hints: Contrast pond 2 with pond 1 - low density, plenty of food for all, and now intermediates are commonest. Which phenotype is being favoured this time?
Look back at what intermediates can eat compared with the specialists. Why is being able to eat detritus, algae and shrimp all together helpful when there is no shortage?
Recall the name for selection that favours the average / middle phenotype and removes extremes, and link it to low competition and better growth on a varied diet.
walkthrough:
Picture Life in Pond 2**
Now imagine few tadpoles with plenty of all foods. There is little competition, so there is no pressure to be the absolute fastest specialist. Survival depends on growing well on what is available.

Why the Middle Wins Here**
Intermediates have teeth-like mouthparts and medium jaws and intestines, so they can eat detritus, algae and fairy shrimp. That broad, varied diet gives better nutrition for growth and development than a narrow specialist diet, so intermediates survive best and extremes are selected against.

Naming the Pattern**
When the intermediate phenotype is favoured and both extremes decrease, this is stabilising selection. It keeps the population centred on the average and is possible because low density prevents intense competition.

Final answer: Stabilising selection; intermediates are selected for / survive and extremes (detritus feeders and carnivores) are selected against / die; due to low competition; intermediates can eat a wider range of foods and greater variety improves growth and development.

hints: In pond 2 most tadpoles are intermediates with medium intestines and few have very short or very long intestines. What smooth symmetrical shape shows most individuals clustered around the mean for a continuously varying trait?
walkthrough:
Linking Variation to Shape**
Intestine length shows continuous variation because it is controlled by many genes plus environment, ranging from short in carnivores to long in detritus feeders. In pond 2 most individuals are intermediates, with fewer and fewer toward either extreme, so number of tadpoles plotted against length gives a symmetrical bell with a central peak.
Final answer: Single bell-shaped normal distribution curve peaking at intermediate / mean intestine length.

hints: Think about what the word sympatric means for geography - unlike a mountain or river splitting a population, where do the diverging groups live?
If they live together, what must stop them interbreeding so that the carnivore and detritus-feeder gene pools split into new species? Think ecological or behavioural differences.
walkthrough:
Same Place, Separate Species**
Sympatric means in the same place. There is no geographical barrier. The tadpoles live in the same pond, so speciation must happen without physical separation.

How Isolation Still Happens**
New species form only when gene flow stops. Here isolation is ecological or behavioural, for example feeding in different parts of the pond, breeding at different times, or mating only with the same feeding type. Over time mutations accumulate separately and the groups become reproductively isolated and cannot produce fertile offspring together.
Final answer: Formation of new species due to reproductive isolation; caused by ecological / behavioural separation in the same geographical region.

hints: To build the tree in Fig. 7.3 scientists need a molecule that all three toads share but that changes over time. Which molecule would you sequence and compare?
Once you have the sequences, what do you count between species, and what does a small count versus a large count tell you about how recently they shared an ancestor?
Look at Fig. 7.3 to see which two species share the most recent branch point about 15 million years ago, then explain how DNA data plus databases would confirm they are closest.
walkthrough:
Comparing the Same Code**
Sequence the same gene or whole genome DNA from S. multiplicata, S. hammondii and S. bombifrons. Because mutations accumulate over time, the nucleotide sequence acts like a molecular clock.

Counting Differences to Find Relatedness**
Align the sequences with software such as BLAST and count base differences. The fewer the differences, the more closely related the species and the shorter the time since they diverged from a common ancestor.

Reading the Tree**
Analysis shows S. hammondii and S. bombifrons have the fewest genetic differences, so they share the most recent common ancestor about 15 million years ago, while S. multiplicata split off earlier about 30 million years ago. That is why they are placed as sister branches in Fig. 7.3.

Final answer: Obtain DNA sequences for the three species; count / compare nucleotide / base differences / similarities using bioinformatics / databases / BLAST; fewer differences means more closely related / less time since divergence; S. hammondii and S. bombifrons are most similar.
